rationale: Python 3.14 semantics, fully static: functools.partial stores its fixed positional argument objects in partial.args at construction time. Inside make_partial, the name ARGV resolves against module globals when the factory body runs (after ARGV is bound to ["pacman","-S","r22-partial-global"]), so partial.args[0] is that early list object. Rebinding the module global ARGV to the late ["pacman","-Q","r22-partial-global-late"] list after bound = make_partial() creates a second object and never mutates the captured one. bound() therefore invokes run_helper with the construction-time list, and the subprocess.run inside it spawns exactly pacman -S r22-partial-global: one observed host_mutation row, zero unparsed, so expected_kind is exact. A detector that folds a returned partial's fixed argument in the invocation environment (the F1 same-class defect for functools.partial noted in the r21 review) reports the late rebound value pacman -Q r22-partial-global-late as a package_query; that serialization is the named discriminator in forbid_observed_commands. -Q and -S against the invented names are inert markers only; no cell is ever executed.
